title: Indian EO Startup SatSure Raises $21M, With Sovereign Fund Investment
summary: Indian Earth observation startup SatSure raises 21 million dollars with sovereign fund
detailed: Earth Observation company SatSure raised a $21 million Series B round in a mix of equity, debt, and secondary transactions, with investment from India’s sovereign space-technology fund.

SatSure, based in Bengaluru, India, plans to use the capital to advance its optical payloads ahead of orbital flight in 2027 and for its work on the Indian national EO constellation, which it is a partner in.
India’s sovereign space-tech fund Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF) led the round with a $6.4 million investment.
We built SatSure to own that full stack end to end, and this round lets us build it further, from India, for the world,” said Prateep Basu, CEO and co-founder of SatSure.
sentences: Earth Observation company SatSure raised a $21 million Series B round in a mix of equity, debt, and secondary transactions, with investment from India’s sovereign space-technology fund.

SatSure, based in Bengaluru, India, plans to use the capital to advance its optical payloads ahead of orbital flight in 2027 and for its work on the Indian national EO constellation, which it is a partner in.
SatSure announced the round on Nov.
20, stating it includes $17.6 million in equity; $2.7 million in venture debt, and $1.1 million in secondary transactions.
India’s sovereign space-tech fund Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF) led the round with a $6.4 million investment.
AVCF is anchored by the national space regulator IN-SPACe and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited.
SatSure owns subsidiary KaleidEO, which builds optical satellite payloads.
KaleidEO has demonstrated its optical, multispectral payload in aerial tests but has not yet launched a satellite.
SatSure develops AI and foundational models that deliver insights from its imagery, giving the company capabilities across the value chain.
“The strategic value of the space economy lies not only in reaching orbit, but in what we can understand from it.
That intelligence is reliable only when you own the full chain behind it, from the payloads in orbit to the AI and foundation models that turn data into decisions.
We built SatSure to own that full stack end to end, and this round lets us build it further, from India, for the world,” said Prateep Basu, CEO and co-founder of SatSure.
